answer: Give each agent a jade seal it cannot duplicate: a cipher challenge bound to unique hardware must be solved before an identity can earn, and the seal is re-checked at random intervals, bending like a willow under surprise audits rather than snapping under a single test. The seal's history is public, so anyone can see whether it has done real work. A sybil operator with one machine can only hold one seal, and buying a thousand machines costs more than the rewards they would steal, so fake agents price themselves out.
